I am 63 years old and I never went to school. I cannot read the words on the fertilizer bags, but I know my land because I have been farming it since I was a girl. My family has 8 mu in Quzhou. Every year, I plant wheat in October and maize in June right after the wheat comes off. That is what my neighbors do and that is what my mother did. I also keep 1.5 mu for cotton because my neighbor across the road gets good money for it, and I need cash for my medicine.

For wheat, I hire the tractor man to rotary till before planting. I sow about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu. I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant, and another bag later when the wheat starts to grow fast. I also spread ammonium bicarbonate because that is what I have always done. I irrigate three times — winter, jointing, and filling — because the well water is there and I would rather waste a little water than lose the crop. I spray four times for weeds and bugs. If the weather is normal, I should get about 1000 jin per mu.

For maize, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest. We only have five or six days before it is too late. I plant hybrid maize seed directly, no-tillage. The hybrid seed costs more but it grows strong. I use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Two irrigations are enough for maize. I spray three times for pests.

For cotton, I rotary till and sow improved cotton seed. Cotton needs a lot of work — I spray eight times because the bollworms are trouble every year. I irrigate twice. I hope for 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I do not count kilograms. I count bags. But my son told me the extension man said my wheat gets about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu from all that fertilizer. I just buy what I can afford and what the shopkeeper recommends.
